articles.body: I've done a lot of QA automation interviews on both sides of the table. The best signal I ever got from a candidate was not a Q&A answer. It was watching them open a broken suite and work out why it was broken. So I built a few small practice projects for that. Each one is a tiny app plus a Playwright suite with several seeded problems. Some are test bugs, some are config bugs, and some are real bugs in the app that the tests were right about. Part of the exercise is deciding which is which.

articles.title: How we keep a social media scheduler from double-posting: a 200-process contention test
articles.excerpt: A social media scheduler has one job it must never get wrong: publish a post once. If two workers wake up for the same scheduled item at the same moment, a naive scheduler posts twice, and a duplicate…
articles.body: A social media scheduler has one job it must never get wrong: publish a post once. If two workers wake up for the same scheduled item at the same moment, a naive scheduler posts twice, and a duplicate on a client's account is worse than a late post. In Cascads, a multi-brand social media cockpit, the guard is a durable claim: for one content item and one network key, exactly one process may call the provider while the claim is active. We wanted evidence that this holds under real contention, not just a passing unit test, so we measured it. Method Each round follows the same five steps: Create a new temporary ledger for the round. Start 8 independent Node.js processes and hold them at a common barrier. Release the barrier so every process contests the same item and platform key.

articles.title: Turning a 3D printer part's chamfers back into parameters you can edit
articles.excerpt: mesh2cad takes an STL and gives back CAD: a STEP file with real planes, cylinders and cones, and, when the part is simple enough, a CadQuery or OpenSCAD script with named parameters. The point of the…
articles.body: mesh2cad takes an STL and gives back CAD: a STEP file with real planes, cylinders and cones, and, when the part is simple enough, a CadQuery or OpenSCAD script with named parameters. The point of the script is that you can open it and change hole_1_d instead of fighting triangles. I test on six real Original Prusa i3 MK3S printer parts. Yesterday's post got five of them to exact STEP. 0.12.0 does two things: it sews the last one, and it makes the belt idler editable as a script. The last STEP: a bore that meets everything On y-rod-holder every surface was already fitted in 0.11.0, but the solid didn't close. The R=4.00 mm rod bore is one cylinder band whose boundary loop touches several planes and the coaxial 45 degree chamfer circles at both ends.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built I got the idea from the MLH Discord. People were asking about account names, missing offer codes and student benefits. Different people, same questions. The useful answer was often already there, just lurking in another thread. I built ThreadSherpa to take over that bit of repetitive work. A moderator answers a question in the usual way, then right-clicks their reply and selects Apps → Save this answer . When someone asks a similar question in a connected support forum, the bot uses those saved facts to write a short reply for that person, with a link back to the original. In my test server, a moderator saves: Keep the same repo link and push your fixes in before the submissions close.

articles.title: Sellers: what proof do you actually send besides the file itself?
articles.excerpt: Last month I watched the same argument play out three times in agent/freelance marketplaces: Seller: "I delivered exactly that file." checks screenshots, shrugs Payment has been solved three times ove…
articles.body: Last month I watched the same argument play out three times in agent/freelance marketplaces: Seller: "I delivered exactly that file." Buyer: "That's not what I received / not what I ordered." Platform: checks screenshots, shrugs Payment has been solved three times over — escrow, x402, instant USDC. Delivery evidence is still screenshots and vibes. And reputation isn't filling the gap: in a 2026 study of the ERC-8004 registry, after Sybil filtering, 86.8% of "rated" agents had no valid feedback left. So I built the smallest possible fix and shipped it: ProofReceipt ( https://proofreceipt.netlify.app ). Before you send a deliverable, you paste/drop it in, and it seals a SHA-256 receipt binding seller + client + job + amount + the deliverable itself.

articles.body: Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21.

articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

articles.title: Private Griffin moon lander gets put to the test | Space photo of the day for Oct. 23, 2026
articles.excerpt: The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year.
articles.body: The Griffin-1 lunar lander undergoes testing at NASA's Jet Propulsion Lab. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The robotic Griffin lunar lander has passed a host of critical tests ahead of its first-ever moon mission, which is scheduled to launch later this year. What is it? At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1 ) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. The spacecraft was put through environmental testing that explored how the vehicle will fare in the extreme conditions it will experience on its ride to the surface of the moon . This testing simulated the extreme temperatures, shaking and even the sounds that the spacecraft will experience from launch to landing.

articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

articles.title: Rocket Lab launches 3 'Hawk' satellites to orbit to gather signals intelligence
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 21), the 19th mission of the year for the California-based company.
articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.
